messages.subject: ETA accuracy question
messages.body:
Samir,

A procedural question from our side. Our planners compare the Parcelwise ETA against actual delivery time and see a deviation of roughly 12 minutes on afternoon routes. Can you confirm whether the ETA is calculated at dispatch or recalculated en route?

I need this documented for our internal quality file. Please reply with specifics, not marketing language.

Kind regards,
Carla Dunne
Head of Operations, Swiftbox

messages.subject: Re: ETA accuracy question
messages.body:
Hi Carla,

Good question - the ETA is calculated at dispatch and then recalculated whenever the driver's app syncs position (roughly every 30-60 seconds, depending on connectivity). So afternoon deviations usually mean sync gaps in areas with poor coverage rather than the calculation itself.

If you tell me which routes showed the 12-minute deviation I can ask our team to check the sync logs for those days. No promises on what we'll find, but it's worth a look.

Best,
Samir

messages.subject: scanner trouble in the rain
messages.body:
Hi there Jonas,

Walt Pruitt over at Harbor Express. One of my drivers, Gus, says the scanner won't read barcodes when the app is in rain mode - he swears the screen goes dim as a church basement. He had to type three tracking numbers by hand in Tuesday's downpour and he's still grumbling about it.

messages.subject: Re: scanner trouble in the rain
messages.body:
hi walt,

yes, rain mode intentionally dims the screen and locks touch input so raindrops don't trigger ghost taps. scanning should still work though - if the camera can't focus in the dim mode that's a bug, not a feature.

have gus try: rain mode on, scan a barcode, and note if the red focus line appears. if it doesn't, tell me the app version from settings and i'll look. 30 seconds of work for him, saves me an hour of guessing.

messages.subject: Re: duplicate webhooks - what do i tell the customer?

messages.subject: prospect wants EU data residency in writing
messages.body:
Hola Helen, hola Ingrid!

A prospect (mid-size, ~40 drivers) asked for written confirmation that all their data stays in the EU before they'll sign. I'm 95% sure we already say this somewhere, but where? Is it in the standard contract or only on the website?

I promised them an answer by Wednesday, so a simple 'yes, point them to clause X' works great for me ✅

Saludos,
Tomás

messages.subject: Re: prospect wants EU data residency in writing
messages.body:
Dear Tomás,

Thank you for asking before promising anything in writing, I do appreciate that. Our hosting is within the EU and this is stated on the website; however, the standard contract does not yet contain an explicit residency clause. I would gently suggest pointing the prospect to the website statement for now, and I can ask our legal adviser whether a short confirmation letter would be appropriate.

Kind regards,
Helen Oyelaran
CFO, Parcelwise B.V.
